script.text: Reportedly, the U.S. and Israel are planning new Iran strikes. Why wait until November?

The New York Times reports that American and Israeli planners have drawn up options for a short, intense campaign against Iran. Targets under discussion are nuclear sites, energy infrastructure, and missile and drone systems.

The reported window opens in early November, after the U.S. midterm elections. Officials say no final decision has been made, and President Trump has not authorized an operation. The Financial Times reported that he opposed an Israeli strike planned for around October tenth.

Some officials believe a concentrated campaign could pressure Tehran into concessions. Iran has threatened data centers, undersea internet cables, and Saudi oil refineries. Iranian officials say there are no talks until Washington lifts sanctions.
Will the U.S. strike Iran again before January? Yes or no?

upload.title: Iran: US and Israel Reportedly Plan New Strikes #shorts
upload.description:
The New York Times reports that U.S. and Israeli planners have drawn up options for a short, intense campaign against Iran, with nuclear sites, energy infrastructure and missile and drone systems among the targets under discussion. According to the reports, the window would open in early November, after the U.S. midterm elections. Officials say no final decision has been made, and President Trump has not authorized a new operation. The Financial Times reported that Trump opposed an Israeli strike that was planned for around October 10. Some officials believe a concentrated campaign could pressure Tehran into concessions. Iran has threatened to hit data centers, undersea internet cables and Saudi oil refineries; Iranian officials say there will be no talks until Washington lifts sanctions. The reports rely on anonymous officials and have not been confirmed by either government.
